sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1916. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Part I: Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group: Specimens of Western Hindi and Panjabi. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. Pp. 550-556 ("Dialects of Central Chhindwara"; "Gaoli, Raghobansi, and Kirari" and specimen No. 27 "Bundeli (Gaoli), District Chhindwara", pp. 554-555)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. The only primary linguistic statement on the Gaoli/Gowli caste speech: "From the account originally given of Gaoli, Raghobansi, and Kirari, it was at the time concluded that they were most probably forms of Malwi. An examination of the specimens since obtained will show that they are all merely impure Bundeli." (p. 550-551) and "These are the dialects of the castes implied by their names. They are all reported from Chhindwara.. Gaoli 16,093.. As a matter of fact, they in no way differ from the ordinary broken Bundeli of the district." (pp. 554-555), followed by a Parable sp…

sources.citation: Russell, R. V. & Hira Lal. 1916. The Tribes and Castes of the Central Provinces of India, Vol. III. London: Macmillan. Article "Gowari", pp. 160-165 (Project Gutenberg ebook 41424)
sources.note: Nothing; ethnographic caste article ("The herdsman or grazier caste of the Maratha country, corresponding to the Ahirs or Gaolis"); no statement on language at all, let alone stress.

sources.citation: Hammarström et al. Glottolog 5.x, languoid gowl1241 "Gowli" [gok] (md.ini, tree/book1242/gowl1241) — the parent language of Multitree's gok-nan
sources.note: Nothing on stress. hh_ethnologue_comment (comment_type = Spurious): Ethnologue E16-E29 list Gowli [gok] (Madhya Pradesh; Maharashtra, Amravati District; Indo-Aryan, Central zone, Western Hindi, Unclassified) and Gowlan [goj]; both refer to the Gowari/Gaoli/Gowli caste, and "on purely linguistic grounds, both are spurious, since the Gowli do not have a language that is mutually unintelligible with all surrounding languages (Grierson LSI 9:I: 554-555, Russell & Hiralal: Gowari)". altnames multitree = Gowli, Nand. Sources: Gunthorpe 1888, Russell & Hiralal 1916.

sources.note: Nothing. Record is: name = Nand; level = language; macroareas = Eurasia; countries empty; [altnames] multitree = Nand; [identifier] multitree = gok-nan. No sources, no classification, no coordinates. Web page adds only the standard retirement notice.

sources.citation: LINGUIST List. MultiTree: a digital library of language relationships, CLDF dataset (github.com/linguistlist/multitree), tables
sources.note: Nothing. row: gok_nan, Nand, Glottocode nand1263. : gok_nan "Nand", Node_Type Dialect under gok "Gowli" (Geography "India: Madhya Pradesh; Maharashtra, Amravati District.") in trees 14596 (Source Ethnologue15, Gordon 2005), 19655 (LINGUIST List integrated) and 21328 (Ethnologue 16, Lewis 2009). So "Nand" is an Ethnologue-15/16 dialect name for Gowli [gok]; no linguistic source attached.

sources.note: The only full descriptive study of Bundeli, the language Grierson identifies the Gaoli/Gowli caste speech with; if a stress rule for the speech behind 'Nand' exists anywhere, it is here. Belongs to bund1253, not to nand1263, which should simply be closed as spurious.
